decisions.option: A (the review's recommended option, not yet confirmed by the owner): two rows of five and four where the nine coding keys would be under about 40 px wide, as a CSS container query on the keypad.
decisions.what_changed: Keypad.svelte gets an optional `narrowColumns` prop (used only with `columns`). With it the keypad is a wrapping flex row that is its own query container (`container-type: inline-size`): nine keys share the row (flex 1 1 0) until the keypad is narrower than 24.49rem (nine keys of 40 px and their 4 px gaps = 392 px), then each key takes one fifth of the width (less 1 px, so rounding never drops the fifth key) and the other four wrap to a second row, centred. The query follows the keypad's own width, so it also reacts to text size (rem) and to narrow windows, not only to phones; a browser without container queries keeps the old one row. CodingRenderer passes narrowColumns=ceil(9/2)=5. The gap of the coding keypad on phones is 0.25rem (was 0.125rem): the folded rows need a gap a finger can aim at, and the 412 px Pixel's keys would be 38.7 px with it, so that phone folds too. The coding response path is unchanged: same nine <button>s in the same order, same `press` handler, `responseTimestampFromEvent` and block clock (section 11.6); only the layout differs. The digit span keypad (no `columns`) is byte-for-byte the same markup, classes and style attributes as before; NumericEntry does not use the Keypad.

deviations: The fold threshold is stated as 'keys under about 40 px'; with the 4 px phone gap it falls at a keypad width of 392 px (viewport about 424 px), so a 412 px phone (keys would be 38.7 px) is folded, where with the old 2 px gap it had 40.4 px keys. 430 px and wider phones keep one row of 40.7 px keys.
The coding keypad's phone gap went from 2 px to 4 px (also unfolded, on 424 to 480 px viewports). Keys unfolded at 430 px are 40.7 px wide, as before to within a pixel.
The second row (four keys) is centred, not left-aligned: 6 sits between 1 and 2. A left-aligned row is a one-line change (justify-content) if the owner prefers digits to line up in columns.

The folded keypad adds 54 px of height (block 302 px against 248 px). The 320 x 568 and 390 x 664 screens fit it with room to spare (the test budget is 468 px); the shortest phone's visible Safari area is not measured here.
open_issues: Browsers without container queries (Safari before 16.0, about 1 percent) keep the one row, which is today's layout.

Layout only: the response path was not re-timed on a device. The block's timing code (CodingRenderer script) is unchanged; section 11.6 recommends a re-check on a real phone for any change to a timed block.

decisions.option: A (the review's recommended option, since no norms are collected yet; not yet confirmed by the owner): the fixation '+' is drawn centred in the pad and the separate fixation row is gone.
decisions.what_changed:
RtRenderer markup and CSS only. The `.fixation`

moved from a row above the pads into `.pads` (now position: relative) and is drawn absolutely over it (inset 0, grid, place-items centre, z-index 1, pointer-events: none), still aria-hidden, still '+' only while the trial is in its fixation state and '' otherwise; its 2.5rem row height and the stage's 0.75rem gap are gone, so the stage is 52 px (3.25rem) shorter: 228 px high with one position (was 280). One position: the cross is in the middle of the one pad (measured offset 0 to 0.5 px from the pad's middle at 320 and 390 px in all three engines). Four positions: the cross is in the middle of the row of pads, which is the gap between pads 2 and 3 (the four pads are exactly as before, equal and in one row). The script section is unchanged: trial state machine, rAF onset scheduler, performance.now(), response stamping, the practice/main stages. The target replaces the cross in the same flush as before (the pad box does not move: tested). A tap on the cross reaches the pad (elementFromPoint at the cross is the pad; pointer-events none).
tests: rt.dom.test: the cross is a child of .pads, aria-hidden, the stage has no row above the pads (children pads [+ keys]), and the target frame empties it (new); snapshot 2 (choice4 fixation) updated

e2e/uxdec-render.spec.ts: one position at 390 and 320 px (cross within 1.5 px of the pad's middle horizontally and 2.5 px vertically, the pad starts at the top of the stage, pointer-events none, a tap on the cross reaches the pad, the stage fits the screen, the pad does not move when the target appears); four positions on the dev-only review page (needs HB_DEV_SERVER=1); axe at 390 px, light and dark
RT self-test checks, see gates: e2e/rt-selftest.spec.ts (8 tests per engine) and src/selftest unit tests, all green
deviations: With four positions 'centred in the pad' has no single pad: the cross is centred on the row, in the gap between the middle two pads, and overlaps their inner borders by about 4 to 7 px. A halo in the stage's own colour (text-shadow, 2 px) keeps it legible over the borders. A cleaner option would be an extra middle slot that moves pads 2 and 3 apart (changes the stimulus spacing, so it was not done).
open_issues: The RT self-test page (rt-selftest.html, src/selftest) measures the device (frames, timers, key and tap latency) and does not mount RtRenderer, so its green result shows that the device checks are unaffected, not that the renderer's timing was re-measured. The renderer's timing path (script) is unchanged and rt.dom.test (onset frame, RT from the onset frame, anticipations, event timestamps) passes.

Pre-existing, not changed: the four pads wrap 3+1 when the stage is narrower than 4 x 3rem plus gaps (on the dev review page at 320 px, and at 200% text between about 460 and 530 px viewport width). The cross then sits at the middle of the whole pad grid, which is over a pad edge in the 3+1 case. At 200% text on phones the pads wrap 2+2 and the cross is at the crossing of the four pads.

This package routed its own specs through the new e2e/uxdec-render-flow.ts (same walk, answers the offer); when routes.ts is fixed, the ux-render/ux2-render imports can go back to './routes' and uxdec-render-flow.ts can be deleted.
